claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands accept `executionMode` and `pipelineType` settings for a pipeline definition.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link to AWS CodePipeline docs concepts-how-it-works.html documents CodePipeline execution mode.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines YAML supports a `lockBehavior` property set at the stage level that controls how runs are handled against an exclusive lock check on a referenced environment.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`; the alternative is `sequential`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time, in the same way as `sequential` lock behavior.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The Pulumi@1 Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args`.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one run.
When two concurrent builds target the same stack, the second build's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The link /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as a page describing update conflicts.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option is named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" and is located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
With the TeamCity limit set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only after it finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, serializing Pulumi deployments is done by adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive lock proceed in sequence (queued one at a time).
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1 serializes deployments.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
